item.title: Regex Bypass - Escaping WebView Domain Filters
item.description: An Android deeplink validation bypass that allowed loading arbitrary domains in the app’s WebView through regex pattern mismatches.

item.title: data:text/html;base64 URLs to bypass webView filters
item.description:
I was testing this app com.testapp.android which had a deeplink testapp://webview/?url=https://testapp.com. It allowed only certain URLs to be passed to the url= parameter. Most of the time I usually start with simple google.com or example.com just to see if the app has proper whitelisting or they are blocking based on some other filtering.

bash
adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "testapp://webview/?url=https://google.com" com.testapp.android

Trying the command above failed, so it looked like there was some URL filtering. Just to throw things at the wall, I tried schemes other than https such as file:// and data:text/html. For the file:// URI the app just opened the default/Home view of the app. But the data:text/html scheme worked. The app placed all the content of the URI in the webview URL bar and showed the content as well.

item.title: Gaining access to protected components
item.description:
In the previous post I talked about what activities are and how we can exploit exported activities. In this post, I’ll show you how an attacker might be able to access the components which are protected i.e not exported. And in the end, I’ll show you how I found one of the similar bugs on a public bug-bounty program.

What is this vulnerability?

Basically what happens is that an activity(let’s call it A) accepts some extras. Those could be simple string(getStringExtra) or could be a parcerable. And without any sort of verification it passes the content of those extra to trigger(startActivity). So Activity A ends up starting a new activity which was given by the user via those extras.

item.title: Exploiting Exported activities in Android apps
item.description: This blog post doesn’t teach you the very basics of the android app, it just talks about the exported activity and their exploitation
